children: Nvidia-backed data-center operator Firmus will supply OpenAI with computing capacity from two planned data centers in Malaysia, as demand for advanced artificial intelligence and infrastructure in the region continues to surge.
The multiyear deal with OpenAI for the AI factory sites  will make the ChatGPT developer an anchor customer, Australia's Firmus said Tuesday.
The company didn't disclose the value of the contract, but said the agreement takes Firmus's total contracted capacity to more than 900 megawatts.
The addition of Malaysia expands Firmus's Asia-Pacific presence beyond Australia, Singapore and Indonesia. It plans to deploy Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI processors at scale across the region.
Two AI factory sites are operational in Australia and Singapore, while five are under development with ready-for-service targets set over the next 24 months, Firmus said.
Shares of Maas Group, an Australia-listed investor in Firmus, rose 4.2% following the announcement.
"These new data centers in Malaysia will help us serve growing demand for OpenAI's products across the region and around the world," said Sachin Katti, vice president of compute strategy at OpenAI.

Founded in 2019, Firmus's new equity raised over the past year topped $3 billion, valuing the company at more than $10.5 billion. It has attracted major investors including Jane Street, Blackstone and Coatue.

Malaysia is experiencing significant growth as one of Southeast Asia's fastest-growing data center markets, drawing billions of dollars in investments from global companies including Microsoft and Google.

"AI infrastructure demand is accelerating across Asia-Pacific, and meeting it requires full-stack AI factories engineered for performance, durability, efficiency, scale and fungible workloads," said Nico Caprez, vice president of global AI infrastructure growth at Nvidia.
